items.title: `tl.cat` fails with misleading errors when operands differ along `dim`, despite its assertion allowing it
items.body:
## Summary The `can_reorder=False` path of `tl.cat` was introduced in #9312 and is implemented as a `join → permute → reshape` decomposition. After #11293 removed CatOp, this is the only implementation left. Its precondition assertion follows the input contract of `torch.cat` — all dims except `dim` must match, and the dim itself is allowed to differ: ```python # python/triton/language/core.py assert all(input.shape[i] == other.shape[i] for i in builtins.range(rank) if i != dim), f"tensor dims must match except in the concat dimension {dim}, ..." ``` However, any input that differs along `dim` fails to compile, and the error never mentions `cat`: it comes from the broadcast inside `join` or from the shape check inside `reshape`, so nothing points back to the call site. The commit message of #9312 states "I also fixed `tl.cat` to be equivalent in semantics to `torch.cat`" — that equivalence only holds when both inputs already have the same shape. ## Reproducer ```python import pytestl import torch import triton import triton.language as tl @pytest.mark.parametrize("m1, m2", [ pytest.param(16, 8, id="non_broadcastable"), pytest.param(1, 8, id="broadcastable"), ]) def test_cat_shape_mismatch(m1, m2): @triton.jit def kernel(X, Y, M1: tl.constexpr, M2: tl.constexpr): x = tl.load(X + tl.arange(0, M1)) y = tl.load(Y + tl.arange(0, M2)) z = tl.cat(x, y, dim=0) tl.store(X + tl.arange(0, 1), tl.sum(z)) x = torch.zeros(m1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) y = torch.zeros(m2, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) with pytest.raises(triton.CompilationError) as exc_info: kernel[(1, )](x, y, M1=m1, M2=m2) print(str(exc_info.value).splitlines()[-1]) ``` The two inputs that differ along `dim` produce two unrelated errors, and neither mentions `cat`: | Case | Error (a `ValueError` wrapped in `CompilationError`) | Raised by | |---|---|---| | `(16,) + (8,)`, not broadcastable | `Cannot make_shape_compatible: incompatible dimensions at index 0: 16 and 8` | `broadcast_impl_value` inside `join` | | `(1,) + (8,)`, broadcastable | `Shape element 0 must be a power of 2` | `validate_block_shape` inside `reshape` | ## Root cause The first step of the decomposition, `join`, requires both operands to have the same shape at the IR level (`SameTypeOperands`). The frontend aligns the shapes by calling `broadcast_impl_value` — that is broadcast semantics, not concat semantics. Inputs that differ along `dim` therefore fail at one of two different points: 1. **Not broadcastable**: `16 vs 8` cannot be broadcast, so `join` raises `Cannot make_shape_compatible` right away. 2. **Broadcastable**: when one side is `1`, `join` broadcasts it silently (`(1,)` is replicated into `(8,)`, so the data no longer represents a concat). After `permute`, the tensor holds 2×8 = 16 elements. The `reshape` target, however, is computed independently from the original input shapes as `[1+8] = [9]` — the correct size under `torch.cat` semantics. The correct target and the broadcast intermediate result no longer line up, and since `reshape` also requires every dim of its target to be a power of two, `9` fails the check and raises `Shape element 0 must be a power of 2` (`0` is the dim index; the value there is `9`). ```mermaid flowchart TD A["tl.cat(x, y, dim)"] --> B{"shapes identical?"} B -- "yes" --> C["join / permute / reshape
correct result, matches torch.cat"] B -- "no" --> D{"concat dim broadcastable?
(one side is 1)"} D -- "no (e.g. 16 vs 8)" --> E["broadcast_impl_value inside join
Cannot make_shape_compatible: 16 and 8"] D -- "yes (e.g. 1 vs 8)" --> F["join broadcasts silently:
(1,) replicated into (8,)
after permute: 16 elements"] F --> G["reshape target computed from
original inputs is [9]
Shape element 0 must be a power of 2"] ``` More fundamentally, this is not a missing feature — it cannot be implemented at all: the sum of two distinct powers of two is never a power of two, so with different sizes along `dim` the output shape is itself not a legal Triton block shape. Under Triton's model, where every block dimension must be a power of two, no implementation that returns a block tensor can produce it. ## Suggested fix Tighten the assertion in `cat` to require equal shapes on all dims: > `tl.cat requires tensors of the same shape, got [16] and [8]` ## Environment details Triton:main GPU: A100

items.title: `desc.scatter()` emits `tile::scatter4` on consumer Blackwell (sm_12x) and fails in ptxas instead of erroring at compile time
items.body:
On consumer Blackwell (`sm_12x`), `tensor_descriptor.scatter()` is lowered to `tile::scatter4`,
which that target does not implement. Triton emits the instruction anyway, so the failure only
appears when `ptxas` rejects the generated PTX, and it is reported as an internal Triton error
that asks the user to file a bug.

TMA **gather** is unaffected on the same architecture and the same descriptor path — only scatter
is missing. Triton's own test suite already encodes this
(`python/test/unit/language/test_tensor_descriptor.py:1487`):

```python
@pytest.mark.skipif(is_sm12x(), reason="TMA Scatter is not supported on sm120")
def test_tma_scatter(...):
```

but there is no corresponding check in the compiler, so users hit it as a codegen failure.

### Minimal reproducer

```python
import torch, triton
import triton.language as tl

X = Y = 128
BLOCK_X = BLOCK_Y = 32

def alloc_fn(size, align, stream):
    return torch.empty(size, dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")

@triton.jit
def scatter_kernel(out_ptr, in_ptr, idx_ptr, y, X: tl.constexpr, Y: tl.constexpr,
                   BLOCK_X: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_Y: tl.constexpr):
    idx = tl.load(idx_ptr + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_X))
    data = tl.load(in_ptr + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_X)[:, None] * BLOCK_Y + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_Y)[None, :])
    desc = tl.make_tensor_descriptor(out_ptr, [X, Y], [Y, 1], [1, BLOCK_Y])
    desc.scatter(data, idx, y)

triton.set_allocator(alloc_fn)
data = torch.rand((BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
idx = torch.randperm(BLOCK_X, device="cuda").to(torch.int32)
out = torch.zeros((X, Y), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
scatter_kernel[(1,)](out, data, idx, 0, X, Y, BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

### Observed

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/drafts/triton-sm12x-scatter/repro.py", line 67, in <module>
    main()
  File "/home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/drafts/triton-sm12x-scatter/repro.py", line 61, in main
    scatter_kernel[(1, )](sout, data, sidx, 0, X, Y, BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y)
  File "/home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/triton/python/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 371, in <lambda>
    return lambda *args, **kwargs: self.run(grid=grid, warmup=False, *args, **kwargs)
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/triton/python/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 755, in run
    kernel = self._do_compile(key, signature, device, constexprs, options, attrs, warmup)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/triton/python/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 899, in _do_compile
    kernel = self.compile(src, target=target, options=options.__dict__)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/triton/python/triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 327, in compile
    next_module = compile_ir(module, metadata)
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/triton/python/triton/backends/nvidia/compiler.py", line 630, in <lambda>
    stages["cubin"] = lambda src, metadata: self.make_cubin(src, metadata, options, self.target.arch)
                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/triton/python/triton/backends/nvidia/compiler.py", line 613, in make_cubin
    raise PTXASError(error)
triton.runtime.errors.PTXASError: PTXAS error: Internal Triton PTX codegen error
`ptxas` stderr:
ptxas-blackwell /tmp/tmpfwc78yt0.ptx, line 222; error   : Feature '.tile::scatter4' not supported on .target 'sm_121a'
ptxas-blackwell /tmp/tmpfwc78yt0.ptx, line 227; error   : Feature '.tile::scatter4' not supported on .target 'sm_121a'
ptxas-blackwell fatal   : Ptx assembly aborted due to errors
Repro command: /home/yashb98/Downloads/OSS/work/triton/python/triton/backends/nvidia/bin/ptxas-blackwell -lineinfo -v --regAllocOptLevel=2 --gpu-name=sm_121a /tmp/tmpfwc78yt0.ptx -o /tmp/tmpfwc78yt0.ptx.o
```

The `PTXASError` is preceded in stdout by a full dump of the generated PTX and the line
"please share the reproducer above with Triton project." (elided here for length).

### Expected

A compile-time error naming the architecture and the unsupported feature, in the same style as the
other validation already in `descriptor_scatter`, rather than an internal codegen error.

### Controls

Run on the same machine, same session, to rule out a broken environment or broken TMA generally:

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| plain `tl.load` / `tl.store` kernel | pass, max abs err 0.0 |
| `desc.gather(idx, y)` | pass, max abs err 0.0; PTX contains `tile::gather4` |
| `desc.scatter(data, idx, y)` | **fails as above** |

### Diagnosis and a possible fix

`TritonSemantic.descriptor_scatter` (`python/triton/language/semantic.py:1154`) validates block
shape, offset rank, dtype and minimum block size, but not target capability. The same file already
has `_has_native_tma()` (`:1083`), which consults `driver.active.get_current_target()`, so an
architecture predicate fits without new plumbing:

```python
def _has_tma_scatter(self, ):
    # Consumer Blackwell (sm_12x) implements TMA `gather4` but not `scatter4`.
    target = driver.active.get_current_target()
    return not (target.backend == "cuda" and target.arch // 10 == 12)
```

plus one assert at the top of `descriptor_scatter`. Built against `main` on this machine, that
turns the failure into:

```
CompilationError
at 6:4:
    desc = tl.make_tensor_descriptor(out_ptr, [X, Y], [Y, 1], [1, BLOCK_Y])
    desc.scatter(data, idx, y)
    ^
TMA scatter is not supported on consumer Blackwell (sm_12x). TMA gather is supported on this architecture; use regular stores instead.
```

and `python/test/unit/language/test_tensor_descriptor.py -k "gather or scatter"` is unchanged:
85 passed / 204 skipped / 0 failed, both with and without the patch.

The equivalent architecture predicate already exists on the backend side —
`TargetInfo::getReductionTreeArity`
(`third_party/nvidia/lib/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM/TargetInfo.cpp:561`) uses
`computeCapability / 10 == 12` with the comment "Consumer Blackwell lacks ternary forms" — and
`is_sm12x()` in `python/triton/_internal_testing.py` is `get_device_capability()[0] == 12`.

**Where would you prefer the check?** The Python front end as above, or
`AsyncTMAScatterOp::verify` in `lib/Dialect/TritonNvidiaGPU/IR/Ops.cpp`, which currently validates
types and shapes but not target capability. The MLIR location would also cover Gluon and any other
front end. I have the Python version working with a test mirroring the existing `is_sm12x` skips,
and am happy to send whichever you prefer.

One note on testing: your CI runs A100, H100 and GB200, so no runner has consumer Blackwell. A test
for this would be skipped everywhere in CI, exactly like the existing `is_sm12x` skips in that file.

## Environment details

```
Triton: 3.8.0+git3ca155e0, built from source at main @ 3ca155e
        (also reproduced on the 3.7.1 release wheel)
GPU:    NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), compute capability 12.1 (sm_121), 48 SMs
Torch:  2.12.1+cu130
CUDA:   13.0 system toolkit; Triton selects its bundled ptxas-blackwell for arch >= 100
        (V13.3.33 at main, V13.1.80 in the 3.7.1 wheel — both reject tile::scatter4 on sm_121a)
OS:     Linux aarch64, Python 3.12
```

Checked against `main` at `c94564c1` (2026-08-17): `semantic.py` and `test_tensor_descriptor.py`
are byte-identical to the tree built and tested above.

I only have `sm_121`; I do not have an `sm_120` part (e.g. RTX 5090), so the "sm_12x" framing
follows Triton's own `is_sm12x()` helper and the existing skip reason rather than a second
measurement.

items.title: [ClusterBarrierInsertion] Multicast TMA into a memdesc view misses its cluster barrier
items.body:
## Describe the bug

`ClusterBarrierInsertion` misses shared-memory effects whose memdesc is a view, so a multicast TMA copy that writes through a `memdesc_index` does not get a cluster barrier before those bytes are reused.

The effect-collection loop uses `allocation.getBufferIds(value)` (`lib/Dialect/TritonNvidiaGPU/Transforms/ClusterBarrierInsertion.cpp:328`), which reads `valueBuffer` only. `valueBuffer` is keyed on the `ttg.local_alloc` result (`Allocation.cpp:250`), while views such as `ttg.memdesc_index` are recorded in `aliasBuffer` and are only visible through `getAllBufferIdsWithAliases` (`Allocation.h:129-139`). The other three call sites in the same file (`:84`, `:97`, `:163`) use the aliasing version; this one does not, so an effect on a view yields an empty buffer-id list and is entered into neither `syncWriteSlices` nor `syncReadSlices`.

## Reproducer

Two functions that differ only in whether the TMA destination is the allocation or a view of it:

```mlir
#blockedTmaDst = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [1, 4], threadsPerWarp = [4, 8], warpsPerCTA = [4, 1], order = [0, 1], CGALayout = [[1, 0]]}>
#nvmmaTma = #ttg.nvmma_shared<{swizzlingByteWidth = 128, transposed = false, elementBitWidth = 16, CGALayout = [[0, 0]]}>
#barrierEncTma = #ttg.swizzled_shared<{vec = 1, perPhase = 1, maxPhase = 1, order = [0], CGALayout = [[1]]}>
#smem = #ttg.shared_memory

module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 2 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 4 : i32, ttg.target = "cuda:90", "ttg.threads-per-warp" = 32 : i32} {
  tt.func @case_indexed_view_reuse(%desc: !tt.tensordesc<64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma>, %v: tensor<64x128xf16, #blockedTmaDst>) {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : i32
    %true = arith.constant true
    %barrier = ttg.local_alloc : () -> !ttg.memdesc<2xi64, #barrierEncTma, #smem, mutable>
    ttng.init_barrier %barrier, 1 : !ttg.memdesc<2xi64, #barrierEncTma, #smem, mutable>
    %bufs = ttg.local_alloc : () -> !ttg.memdesc<1x64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable>
    %dst = ttg.memdesc_index %bufs[%c0] : !ttg.memdesc<1x64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable> -> !ttg.memdesc<64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable>
    ttng.async_tma_copy_global_to_local %desc[%c0, %c0] %dst, %barrier, %true {multicast} :
        !tt.tensordesc<64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma>, !ttg.memdesc<2xi64, #barrierEncTma, #smem, mutable> -> !ttg.memdesc<64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable>
    ttng.wait_barrier %barrier, %c0 deps %dst :
        !ttg.memdesc<2xi64, #barrierEncTma, #smem, mutable>,
        !ttg.memdesc<64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable>
    ttg.local_dealloc %bufs : !ttg.memdesc<1x64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable>
    %reuse = ttg.local_alloc : () -> !ttg.memdesc<64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable>
    ttg.local_store %v, %reuse : tensor<64x128xf16, #blockedTmaDst> -> !ttg.memdesc<64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable>
    ttg.local_dealloc %reuse : !ttg.memdesc<64x128xf16, #nvmmaTma, #smem, mutable>
    ttg.local_dealloc %barrier : !ttg.memdesc<2xi64, #barrierEncTma, #smem, mutable>
    tt.return
  }
}
```

`triton-opt repro.mlir --allocate-shared-memory -test-print-membar`, on `main` (c346e50c7b):

- with the copy targeting `%dst = ttg.local_alloc` directly: `ttng.cluster_barrier` is emitted between the reuse `ttg.local_alloc` and the `ttg.local_store`
- with the copy targeting `%dst = ttg.memdesc_index %bufs[%c0]` as above: no barrier there

Both the original buffer and the reused one are placed at `allocation.offset = 0`, so they are the same bytes. Since the copy is multicast, the writes from one CTA land in the other CTA's shared memory as well, and the reuse store can overwrite bytes that are still in flight. The `wait_barrier` does not cover this, which the in-tree comments already state (`test/TritonNvidiaGPU/membar-cluster.mlir:684-689`, `:834`).

The strongest evidence that the barrier is wanted is the pass's own behaviour: for the same program with a direct destination it emits one.

## The obvious fix is not enough

Changing `:328` to `getAllBufferIdsWithAliases` makes the missing barrier appear, and the new case passes, but it then trips

```
LLVM ERROR: scratch buffer operations should not have any shared memory dependencies
```

on `@local_gather_subslice_other_cta` in `test/Conversion/tritonnvidiagpu_to_llvm.mlir`. Once views are followed, an op can have both a scratch buffer and explicit shared dependencies, which the check at `:349-354` forbids. `Membar.cpp:293-301` already carries the same check with a carve-out for `LocalAtomicScatterRMWOp`, so the two analyses have drifted apart on this point.

I did not want to guess which ops belong in that carve-out inside a concurrency pass, hence an issue rather than a PR. Happy to send the patch if you tell me the shape you want: extend the carve-out to match `Membar.cpp` plus the gather/scatter ops, or drop the invariant and handle scratch-plus-deps ops uniformly in both analyses.

## Environment details

Triton `c346e50c7bb102f35f04d7200a3bc6194bec4c33`, `triton-opt` built from source, no GPU needed to reproduce.

items.title: AMD compilation crash in TritonAMDGPUPrepareIfCombining
items.body:
### Describe the bug


  A Triton kernel fails to compile on the AMD/HIP backend during `make_ttgir`.
  The same reduced kernel compiles successfully for NVIDIA/CUDA, but fails for
  multiple AMD targets.

  The failure is reported while running the AMD-specific
  `TritonAMDGPUPrepareIfCombining` pass:

  ```text
  error: operand #0 does not dominate this use
          m = ((digit == i) & mask).to(tl.uint32)
                        ^
  note: operand defined here (op in a parent region)
      if cond:
        ^

  error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline
  note: Pipeline failed while executing
  [`TritonAMDGPUPrepareIfCombining` on 'tt.func' operation: @repro_kernel]
  RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```
  This appears independent from previously reported AMD issues involving
  TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers and TritonAMDGPUBlockPingpong:

  - The reproducer does not require tt.pointer_range or pointer specialization
    attributes.
  - AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=0 does not avoid the failure.
  - num_stages=1, 2, 3, and 4 all fail.
  - The reproducer does not use tl.dot.
  - Removing either the first if/else that defines digit, the loop that uses
    digit, or the later guarded if cond store makes the reduced reproducer
    compile.

### Reproducer

  Run this on an AMD/ROCm machine:
```
  import torch
  import triton
  import triton.language as tl


  @triton.jit
  def repro_kernel(switch_ptr, input_ptr, output_ptr, N, bit, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
      values = tl.load(switch_ptr + tl.arange(0, 2))
      zero, one = tl.split(values)
      cond = zero < one

      offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
      mask = offsets < N
      x = tl.load(input_ptr + offsets, mask=mask, other=0)

      if cond:
          digit = (x >> bit) & 255
      else:
          digit = ((x >> bit) & 255) - zero

      local = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.uint32)
      for i in range(0, 256):
          m = ((digit == i) & mask).to(tl.uint32)
          cs = tl.cumsum(m, axis=0) - m
          local += cs * m

      if cond:
          tl.store(output_ptr + local, x * one, mask=mask)


  def main():
      n = 8
      x = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
      y = torch.empty(256, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
      switch = torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

      repro_kernel[(1,)](
          switch,
          x,
          y,
          n,
          0,
          BLOCK=256,
          num_warps=4,
          num_stages=3,
      )
      torch.cuda.synchronize()
      print("compiled and ran")


  if __name__ == "__main__":
      main()
```


### Environment details

- Triton: 3.7.1
- GPU:AMD Instinct MI308X

items.title: [Membar] No barrier between a caller's pending shared access and a callee's first one
items.body:
## Describe the bug

The membar analysis models a `tt.call` only by the callee's **exit** state, so the caller's pending shared-memory accesses are never checked against what the callee does **first**. When the two overlap, no barrier is emitted and the accesses race.

`MembarAnalysis::update` takes the callee's summary from `funcMap` (`lib/Analysis/Membar.cpp:250-262`), and that map holds the joined exit state only (`include/triton/Analysis/Function.h:131-154`). A callee whose first shared access is a write therefore looks, at the call site, like whatever it left behind at the end. `getScratchBufferId` also deliberately excludes `triton::CallOp` (`Membar.cpp:131-137`), so the call is not modelled as a scratch op either. Nothing is emitted before the call.

The reverse direction is handled: `test/Analysis/test-membar.mlir:1497-1500` already asserts that a scratch op placed **after** a call, aliasing the call frame, needs a barrier. Moving that scratch op **before** the call exposes the gap.

## Reproducer

```mlir
#blockedCallSrc = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [1, 32], threadsPerWarp = [32, 1], warpsPerCTA = [4, 1], order = [0, 1]}>
#mmaCall = #ttg.nvidia_mma<{versionMajor = 2, versionMinor = 0, warpsPerCTA = [4, 1], instrShape = [16, 8]}>
#blockedCallDst = #ttg.dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mmaCall, kWidth = 2}>
#smem = #ttg.shared_memory

module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 1 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 4 : i32} {
  // First shared access in the callee is the convert_layout's store.
  tt.func private @callee_writes_first() -> tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallDst> {
    %cst = arith.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallSrc>
    %cvt = ttg.convert_layout %cst : tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallSrc> -> tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallDst>
    tt.return %cvt : tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallDst>
  }

  tt.func @caller_pending_read_then_call() -> tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallDst> {
    %cst = arith.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallSrc>
    %cvt = ttg.convert_layout %cst : tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallSrc> -> tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallDst>
    %call = tt.call @callee_writes_first() : () -> tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallDst>
    %sum = arith.addf %call, %cvt : tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallDst>
    tt.return %sum : tensor<128x32xf16, #blockedCallDst>
  }
}
```

```
triton-opt repro.mlir --allocate-shared-memory -test-print-membar
```

Output on `main` (c346e50c7b), caller body:

```mlir
  tt.func @caller_pending_read_then_call() -> ... {
    %cst = arith.constant dense<0.000000e+00> : tensor<128x32xf16, #blocked>
    %0 = ttg.convert_layout %cst {allocation.offset = 0 : i32, allocation.size = 8192 : i32} : ...
    %1 = tt.call @callee_writes_first() {allocation.offset = 0 : i32} : () -> ...
    %2 = arith.addf %1, %0 : ...
    tt.return %2 : ...
  }
```

The caller's scratch is `[0, 8192)` and the call frame starts at the same offset, so the callee's own scratch lands on those bytes. There is no `ttg.barrier local` in the caller.

`ConvertLayoutOpToLLVM` lowers a conversion to store / barrier / load, with a leading barrier only for repeat rounds (`ConvertLayoutOpToLLVM.cpp:208-233`), and `ReduceOpToLLVM` is the same shape. So after the caller's conversion there is an outstanding read of those bytes, and the callee opens with a store to them: one warp can still be reading while another has entered the callee and started writing. The caller's conversion then yields wrong values.

The same hazard inside a single function is caught (`test/Analysis/test-membar.mlir:91-105`), so inlining changes whether the program is correct.

## Reachability

`tt.call` survives to TritonGPU only with `@triton.jit(noinline=True)`, which the in-tree `test_noinline[shared]` already exercises. Any caller that does a layout conversion, a reduction or a `tl.dot` before calling a `noinline` helper is ordinary code.

## Possible fixes

Two shapes, and I would rather not guess which one you want:

1. Conservative: also treat the call as writing its virtual buffer on entry, so any pending caller access that overlaps the frame forces a barrier before the call. Small change, and `tt.call` is rare enough that the extra barriers should be contained, but it is a blunt instrument.
2. Precise: give each function an entry summary alongside the exit one (the accesses before its first synchronization point) and test the caller's pending state against that. Matches what the analysis already does for sync points elsewhere, but it changes the shape of the per-function summary.

Happy to send a PR for whichever you prefer.

## Environment details

Triton `c346e50c7bb102f35f04d7200a3bc6194bec4c33`, `triton-opt` built from source, no GPU needed to reproduce.

items.title: TritonAMDGPUBlockPingpong produces invalid TTGIR with tl.dot, dynamic loop, and runtime-selected pointer
items.body:
### Describe the bug

 A Triton matmul-style kernel fails to compile on the AMD/HIP backend during
  `make_ttgir`. The failure is triggered by a dynamic `tl.range` loop containing a
  runtime `if` that selects one of two B-matrix pointer expressions before a masked
  `tl.load`, followed by `tl.dot`.

  The failure occurs with `num_stages=2` and reports a dominance verifier error
  while executing `TritonAMDGPUBlockPingpong`:

  ```text
Traceback (most recent call last):

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 370, in <lambda>
    return lambda *args, **kwargs: self.run(grid=grid, warmup=False, *args, **kwargs)
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 739, in run
  
    kernel = self._do_compile(key, signature, device, constexprs, options, attrs, warmup)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 884, in _do_compile
    kernel = self.compile(src, target=target, options=options.__dict__)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 327, in compile
    next_module = compile_ir(module, metadata)
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/backends/amd/compiler.py", line 508, in <lambda>
    stages["ttgir"] = lambda src, metadata: self.make_ttgir(src, metadata, options)
                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/backends/amd/compiler.py", line 273, in make_ttgir
    pm.run(mod, 'make_ttgir')
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed

PassManager::run failed
```
  The same reduced reproducer compiles successfully with num_stages=1, which
  suggests the issue is specific to the AMD block-pingpong/pipelining pass rather
  than frontend lowering or pointer canonicalization.
### Reprocuder
Run this on an AMD machine.
```
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def repro_dot_dominance(
    switch_ptr,
    a,
    b,
    c,
    M,
    N,
    K,
    stride_am,
    stride_bn,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
):
    values = tl.load(switch_ptr + tl.arange(0, 2))
    zero, one = tl.split(values)
    cond = zero > one
    m_offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
    k_offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K), tl.float32)

    for n in tl.range(tl.cdiv(N, BLOCK_N)):
        n_offsets = n * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
        a_mask = (m_offsets[:, None] < M) & (n_offsets[None, :] < N)
        a_ptrs = a + m_offsets[:, None] * stride_am + n_offsets[None, :]
        a_block = tl.load(a_ptrs, mask=a_mask, other=0.0)

        b_mask = (n_offsets[:, None] < N) & (k_offsets[None, :] < K)
        if cond:
            b_ptrs = b + n_offsets[:, None] * stride_bn + (one * k_offsets)[None, :]
        else:
            b_ptrs = b + n_offsets[:, None] * stride_bn + k_offsets[None, :]
        b_block = tl.load(b_ptrs, mask=b_mask, other=0.0)

        acc = tl.dot(a_block, b_block, acc, allow_tf32=False)

    c_mask = (m_offsets[:, None] < M) & (k_offsets[None, :] < K)
    c_ptrs = c + m_offsets[:, None] * K + k_offsets[None, :]
    tl.store(c_ptrs, acc, mask=c_mask)


def solve(a, b, c, M: int, N: int, K: int):
    switch = torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device=a.device)
    grid = (1, 1)
    repro_dot_dominance[grid](
        switch, a, b, c, M, N, K, N, K, 32, 32, 32, num_stages=2
    )
```

### Environment details

- Triton: 3.7.1
- AMD Instinct MI308X

items.title: AMD CanonicalizePointers crashes on tt.pointer_range=32 pointer live across control-flow merge with nested early return.
items.body:
### Describe the bug

The AMD TTIR-to-TTGIR pipeline crashes when a small-tensor pointer with
`tt.pointer_range = 32` is derived on both sides of runtime control flow and a
nested path returns before the merge block.

This was first seen in fuzz-generated matrix transpose kernels. The original,
untransformed transpose kernel compiles for AMD with the same runtime pointer
attributes. The transformed variants compile and run on NVIDIA, but AMD fails in
`make_ttgir`.

The failure is not specific to stores: both an output pointer and an input
pointer can trigger it.
### Traceback
```
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 370, in <lambda>
    return lambda *args, **kwargs: self.run(grid=grid, warmup=False, *args, **kwargs)
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 739, in run
    kernel = self._do_compile(key, signature, device, constexprs, options, attrs, warmup)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 884, in _do_compile
    kernel = self.compile(src, target=target, options=options.__dict__)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 327, in compile
    next_module = compile_ir(module, metadata)
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/backends/amd/compiler.py", line 508, in <lambda>
    stages["ttgir"] = lambda src, metadata: self.make_ttgir(src, metadata, options)
                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/backends/amd/compiler.py", line 273, in make_ttgir
    pm.run(mod, 'make_ttgir')
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed

PassManager::run failed
```
  The underlying stderr diagnostic is:

 ```text
  python: .../llvm/ADT/ArrayRef.h:248:
  const T &llvm::ArrayRef<mlir::ValueRange>::operator[](size_t) const
  [T = mlir::ValueRange]:
  Assertion `Index < Length && "Invalid index!"' failed.

  error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline
  note: Pipeline failed while executing
  [`TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers` on 'tt.func' operation: @repro_output_pointer]
```
### Reproduce
Run this on an AMD system:
```
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def repro_output_pointer(switch_ptr, output):
    values = tl.load(switch_ptr + tl.arange(0, 2))
    zero, one = tl.split(values)
    true_cond = zero < one
    false_cond = zero > one
    offsets = tl.arange(0, 32)

    if true_cond:
        output_ptrs = output + offsets + zero
    else:
        output_ptrs = output + offsets
        if false_cond:
            return

    if true_cond:
        tl.store(output_ptrs, offsets)


switch = torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
output = torch.empty(32, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
repro_output_pointer[(1,)](switch, output)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

### Environment details

- Triton: 3.7.1
- AMD Instinct MI308X

items.title: fp8 matmul on sm_120 runs at half the 8-bit rate
items.body:
### Describe the issue

On RTX 50-series cards, an fp8 matmul in Triton reaches only half the speed the tensor cores are
capable of using `tl.dot`.

The hardware has two ways to multiply fp8 into an fp32 accumulator. The one `tl.dot` uses runs at
half rate. The other is the MXFP8 block-scaled instruction that `tl.dot_scaled` uses, and it runs at full rate. If you call `tl.dot_scaled` with all the block scales set to 1.0, you get exactly the plain fp8 matmul back —
the same output as `tl.dot`, bit for bit — and on a 5090 it is 1.55x faster (measured)

My suggestion is to make `tl.dot` use the mxfp8 instruction on sm_120.

This is now done manually here: OneTrainer: [Nerogar/OneTrainer#1686](https://github.com/Nerogar/OneTrainer/pull/1686) —

Apparently also in other packages (AI output, unchecked):
- Dao-AILab QuACK, in CUTLASS DSL:
  [SF fragments filled with 127](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/quack/blob/60d88082272a256fa9b3b2ab631c82cfa78337c6/quack/gemm_sm120.py#L1204-L1251),
  [reasoning](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/quack/blob/60d88082272a256fa9b3b2ab631c82cfa78337c6/quack/gemm_sm120.py#L9-L17).
  Its measurements also show plain unscaled `kind::f8f6f4` matching the Ada-era `mma.sync` (506.4
  vs 507.9 TFLOP/s), so the 2x comes from `.block_scale` and not from the newer instruction as such
- FlashInfer, RFC for MXFP8 attention on SM120:
  [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3628](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3628), with
  the same effect measured in SASS on a 5060 Ti (~102 vs ~202 TFLOP/s)


### Environment details

I don't have those anymore, it was on a cloud. It was a 5060 Ti and a 5090
